why: Abbreviations obscure that we are talking about people.
replace: gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men

suggest: people living with HIV
why: Abbreviations obscure that we are talking about people.

suggest: healthcare workers
why: Abbreviations obscure that we are talking about people.

suggest: people who inject drugs
why: Abbreviations obscure that we are talking about people.

suggest: people experiencing homelessness / people who are homeless
why: Person-first language.

suggest: people living with HIV / people with HIV
why: Person-first language.

suggest: people with intellectual/physical disabilities
why: Person-first language (check preference of the group).

suggest: people with influenza (or 'cases of influenza' if referring to occurrences)
why: 'Case' should refer to the occurrence, not the person. Check context.

suggest: people who use drugs / people with a drug addiction / people who inject drugs
why: Do not define people by a behaviour.

suggest: older adults (define age at first mention) / people over the age of XX
why: Person-first, specific.

suggest: people born outside [country] / outside the reporting country / outside the EU/EEA
why: Othering and not specific.

suggest: people without [disease/condition] / people without underlying conditions
why: Vague and value-laden.

suggest: people with an infection / people who are infectious / people who can transmit the disease
why: Do not refer to people as 'infected'.

suggest: people in prison and/or in detention
why: More person-centred and inclusive of other detained groups.

suggest: sex worker(s)
why: Frames sex work as labour, not a moral failing.

suggest: people with [disease/condition] / people with symptoms
why: Vague; use person-first and specify.

suggest: people who smoke / people who do not smoke / people with a history of smoking
why: Do not define people by a behaviour.

suggest: the affected individual / the person
why: 'Case' used to mean a person is dehumanising.

suggest: [name specific groups] vulnerable to [infection / severe disease]
why: State who and what they are vulnerable to; avoid implying it is inherent.

suggest: groups underserved by / with limited access to healthcare due to …
why: Vague.

suggest: name the group; or 'groups not adequately reached by / facing barriers to accessing healthcare services'
why: Vague and implies the group is the problem.

suggest: Populations such as [name] are at higher risk of [outcome] due to …
why: Name who, what risk, and ideally why.

suggest: populations at lower/higher risk of … / specify
why: Implies a 'norm' versus 'outsiders' when used alongside other groups.

suggest: specific populations
why: 'Sub' can suggest lesser.

suggest: populations not typically affected by …
why: Implies a 'norm'.

suggest: EU residents / EU population / people who live in the EU
why: Excludes non-citizen residents.

suggest: gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (community); 'sex between men' (mode of transmission); 'men in this group' after first mention
why: Avoid reducing a community to a sex act; clarify community vs transmission route.

suggest: pregnant people / vaccination during pregnancy / child born to a vaccinated person
why: Trans men, non-binary and intersex people can also be pregnant.

suggest: refugees / asylum seekers / undocumented migrants / newly arrived migrants / people born outside the reporting country
why: Very broad; be specific.

suggest: undocumented migrants
why: Stigmatising.

pattern: \b(in|across|throughout) (Eastern Europe|Africa|Sub-Saharan Africa|Asia|Latin America|the Middle East|the developing world)\b
suggest: name the specific countries involved
why: Regional generalisations mask differences and reinforce stereotypes.

suggest: name the specific fluids relevant to the pathogen (e.g. blood, semen, vaginal fluid)
why: Be specific.

suggest: define at first use: 'the use of specific psychoactive substances to enhance sexual experiences'
why: Not all readers know the term.

suggest: specify the type of contact
why: Vague.

suggest: sex between men and women
why: Be specific about transmission mode.

suggest: congenital conditions / congenital disorders
why: 'Defect' implies the person is defective.

suggest: population immunity
why: Animal reference is dehumanising.

suggest: engage / prioritise / partner with / serve / tailored to / address / intends to reach; 'priority population', 'intended audience', 'key population'
why: Combative language.

suggest: prompt
why: Combative language.

suggest: contracted / acquired the infection; 'people close to the patient contracted X from the patient'
why: Implies intent or blame.

suggest: adherent / non-adherent / people who do/do not complete treatment
why: Casts patients as passive; mention barriers where known.

suggest: vertical transmission (define at first use)
why: Can sound accusatory.

suggest: behaviour that increases the risk of transmission …; or name the behaviour and why it raises risk
why: Suggests judgement or blame.

suggest: sex without a condom / condomless sex / sex without a condom or other prevention (e.g. PrEP)
why: Suggests fault.

suggest: vaccine acceptance
why: Avoids shaming people for having questions.

suggest: people who drink alcohol heavily / describe settings and barriers instead
why: Blames people or their socio-economic status.
